 :JUDGMENT:
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Akshay Kumar R in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 15.12.2023.
2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 15.12.2023 when the petitioner was proceeding in Activa Honda bearing Reg.No.KA-51-HK-2518 with his friend one Bibin as a pillion rider and when they reached near Chandana TV tower, at that time, respondent's Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-7700 (herein after referred to as SCCH 15 3 MVC No.290/2024 offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle, resulting in the accident.
It is submitted that the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the accident.
3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to AKFA hospital and then he was shifted to Sacred Oak hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In pursuance of service of the notice issued, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their Counsels and filed Objections to the claim petition.

The Respondent No.1 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.1 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-7700 in favour of the respondent No.2.
Without SCCH 15 4 MVC No.290/2024 prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The driver of the said vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
It is submitted by the respondent No.2 that the petitioner himself was tort feasor and Akshay Kumar R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65500863/
2 the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the petitioner.

Hence, on these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

5. Vide order dated 14.05.2024 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES

1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 15.12.2023 at about 3.30 p.m., near Chandana TV Tower, jayamahal main road, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-7700?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3) What Order or Award?

6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 23.
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.290/2024 7.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order
for the following :
REASONS 8. Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 41-7700.
9.

On this point the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 15.12.2023 he being the rider of the Activa Honda bearing Reg.No.KA-51-HK-2518 along with pillion rider was riding slowly and carefully and reached near Chandana TV tower, at Akshay Kumar R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65500863/

10. The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR which discloses that the case has been registered against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence under section 279, 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint given by the petitioner on 18/12/2023.

As far as the delay in lodging the complaint is concerned it is submitted that the petitioner did not have anyone to take care of him and in addition he had no money and hence he got discharged from the hospital and later admitted Sacred Oak Hospital on 17/12/23 and later given his complaint.
Hence the delay in lodging the complaint is in my view satisfactorily explained.

In addition the petitioner has produced ExP4 which is the spot SCCH 15 8 MVC No.290/2024 sketch and the spot mahazar which discloses that the spot of the accident is in front of TV office on the Jayamahal Main Road and the bike was proceedings at its side and the driver of the offending vehicle has gone to the right side of the motor cycle and without noticing the motor cycle has dashed to its right side resulting in the accident.
In addition ExP3 is the charge sheet which discloses that after investigation the charge sheet is filed against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence under section 279, 338 of IPC.
In the investigation also it has been noticed that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
On perusal of the said documents it discloses that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by learned counsel for Respondent and in the cross-examination of PW.1 he stated that he did not observe the goods vehicle before the accident and stated that SCCH 15 9 MVC No.290/2024 the goods vehicle came to his right side and dashed resulting in the accident.

PW1 has denied that the accident he was not having driving license and was not wearing helmet when suggested by the counsel for respondent No 1.
12.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioner side nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also declined the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.

The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 SCCH 15 10 MVC No.290/2024 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver driving the offending vehicle at the Akshay Kumar R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65500863/

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P10 - wound certificate of Sacred Oak hospital that discloses that the petitioner had sustained right elbow fracture and produced Ex.P11 and 12 - Discharge SCCH 15 11 MVC No.290/2024 summaries discloses that he has taken treatment to right ulnar fracture and radial dislocation.
Orif with replating and Ex.P15 are the medical bills and additional medical bills.

As far as the medical bills are concerned PW.1 cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and though it is suggested that PW.1 had sustained only minor injuries however PW.1 has deposed that he has taken further treatment for almost 20 times and denied that the prescriptions did not tally with the medical bills.
It is admitted that the Sl.No.1 in Ex.P15 does not mention his name and Sl.No.4 is in the name of Bipin.
Except suggesting this nothing is elicited in cross-examination of PW.1 to disprove the authenticity of the said medical bills.
Hence excluding the Sl.No.4 bill in view of Ex.P15 the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.4,15,767/- under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P6 discloses that the petitioner has sustained right elbow SCCH 15 12 MVC No.290/2024 fracture and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and he cannot walk, difficulty in manual work, restricted movement in right elbow and lifting objects overhead or do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:

In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 26 years and he was working as Senior field service technician at Aircool systems and earning Rs.50,000/-
p.m.
In support of the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P16 - salary slips for the month of June to November 2023 and Ex.P17 - ID card.
However the SCCH 15 13 MVC No.290/2024 petitioner has not got examined his employer or HR Manager to show that he was drawing the salary of Rs.40,000/- to 50,000/- per month.
In addition the petitioner has not produced his bank account statement to show remittance of the salary to the account of the petitioner.

Since there is no satisfactory evidence to prove the said income and avocation of the petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident, as per the guidelines of Lok-Adalat chart.
As per the relevant period the notional income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least 6 months hence, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.16,000 X 6 = 96,000/- under this head.

The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit he has permanent disability to his right leg.

As per the evidence of PW.3 his impairment is not progressive and will not improve in SCCH 15 14 MVC No.290/2024 future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that he cannot pursue his work as before the accident.

In support of the same, PW.2 - Orthopedic Surgeon is examined and in his evidence he has deposed that the petitioner has healed surgical scar over right forearm, mild pain in right forearm,
difficulty in lifting objects overhead, restricted movements in right elbow flexion and difficult in doing manual work and he has physical disability to right upper limb of 22.57% and to the whole body it would be 11.28%.
He has also deposed that petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant in right ulna for which he has to incur Rs.25,000/-.

As far as disability is concerned PW.2 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 and in his cross-examination PW.2 has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and admitted that the petitioner did not undergo any surgery and his fracture is united.
Except the said suggestions nothing much is elicited in cross-examination of PW.2 to disprove the disability assessed by PW.2.

taking into consideration the disability if taken to the whole body it is just and proper to reduce it to 1/3.

to the whole body.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.16,000/- at the relevant time.
As far as age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P20 the date of the birth of the petitioner is 19.07.1997.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 15.12.2023 was around 26 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi SCCH 15 16 MVC No.290/2024 Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

The loss of future earnings of petitioner due to his above injury and permanent physical disability comes to Rs.2,45,453/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 17 X 7.52%) and the same is awarded to him as compensation under this head.
18. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
19. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have taken the help of an attendant.

Further, he SCCH 15 17 MVC No.290/2024 would be Akshay Kumar R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65500863/

He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.
18. COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
It is stated in the evidence of PW.2 that Petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of the implant and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.25,000/-.
But he has not produced estimation.
However, by considering the need for further surgery, it is proper to grant compensation of 20,000/-.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE  PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid  96,000/-
up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  20,000/-
and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses 4,15,767/-
6. Loss of Future Income 2,45,453/-
7. Future medical expenses  20,000/-
Total 8,47,220/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 8,47,220/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

sentences.text: Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash SCCH 15 19 MVC No.290/2024 and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-7700.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.1, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
22. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 8,47,220/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from SCCH 15 20 MVC No.290/2024 the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the Offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
